Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
708 PM EDT Thu Sep 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 307 PM EDT Thursday...

No major changes to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 307 PM EDT Thursday...

1. Rain to affect portions of our region associated with a 
Nor'easter tracking along New England coast. 

2. Drier and warmer weather will begin the week before more 
shower chances mid week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 307 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure will remain in control of our 
weather across the north country through early Saturday morning.
Tonight will be another cool one with mainly clear skies and 
some fog formation in the valleys, some patchy frost in the 
colder spots of the Adirondacks also. Increasing clouds on 
Friday and into Friday night from the southeast will help to 
prevent both fog and frost formation Friday night. Low pressure 
currently located off the coast of the Carolinas will track 
northeastward, and bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of
the northeast. Our region will be a bit on the periphery of 
this system, but will still have some gusty winds Friday into 
Saturday, and some rain showers Saturday into Saturday night. 
There is still some uncertainty with respect to how far north 
and west the showers spread into our region. Because of this, 
there's some uncertainty with how much precipitation we have. At
this time looks like we could have about half an inch of 
precipitation in Windsor county, and the international border 
could be dry. We will have even less rain in northern New York, 
maybe just a couple tenths of an inch in parts of Essex County, 
New York. Models are also indicating that this Nor'easter is 
likely to have bands of precipitation associated with it, which 
makes it a bit difficult to forecast the precipitation amounts 
and location of the heavier rainfall. There is a strong jet 
associated with this system, which will lead to some gusty 
surface winds. The higher terrain of Vermont and northern New 
York as well as areas around Lake Champlain will have the 
strongest wind gusts. Temperatures will be on the cooler side as
well, especially Sunday as clouds and periods of showers are 
expected, especially across southern and eastern Vermont. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: Any lingering showers from the Nor'easter should
taper off on Monday, though some clouds will likely linger. A 
Bermuda High will shift northwest and attempt to gain influence 
over the region for mid-week, but a cold front will be dropping 
southwest out of Canada. While the cold front will likely 
prevent the warm airmass from being completely established, 
temperatures will likely rise into the 70s and dew points should
rise well into the 50s for much of the region. There will be a 
few showers associated with the front, but no consistent 
rainfall. However, ensemble guidance completely diverges after 
the mid-week, with solutions split between the Bermuda High 
building back and a second cold front pushing through. 
Therefore, the forecast is a blend between the two solutions and
it will likely split one way or the other.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 00Z Saturday...VFR conditions will prevail at all
terminal thru 06z this evening. Expect areas of fog to develop
after 06z, with highest probability (60-80%) of IFR or lower 
conditions at SLK/MPV and EFK. Thinking brief period of IFR
cigs/vis possible again at MSS/BTV toward sunrise on Friday, but
given duration and confidence just mention in tempo group with
this forecast. Thinking the areal coverage and duration of
fog/mist maybe a little less tonight, given large temp/dwpt
spread, slightly stronger winds around 500 feet above ground
level and some high clouds filtering into our region toward
sunrise on Friday. Otherwise, light northeast winds continue
overnight and become 5 to 10 knots with a few higher gusts near
Rutland on Friday with VFR conditions after the fog dissipates
by 14z.
